prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting network collapsed to DONE on the first step (100% of dev episodes), so it scored 0. The cause is the hidden mirror rule. The action for column x lands at column X-dx-x, but a translation-equivariant conv head scores anchor x from features at column x. Its placement scores therefore don't line up with where bricks land. Random placements mostly fill cells outside the target and earn negative reward, so DONE at return 0 wins and training collapses early (mean episode length 1.6 at 25% of training). The first priority is to line up the action head with the landing location. Then I'll test the training recipe and whether a learned column mixing can find the mirror on its own. Every result so far is 0, so there is no noise estimate yet. Anything clearly above 0 on both seeds would be a real signal.

### Round 2
Flipping the trunk features left-right before the pool head is what works. Without it the agent collapsed to DONE (0.000); with it r1c1 scored 0.745 with IoU 0.96. Its training success was still rising at the end (0.38 at 75%, 0.60 at 100%), so it looks short of samples. r1c2 (ppo_epochs 2, ent 0.02, gamma 0.97, 16 minibatches) gave seeds of 0.818 and 0.078: more samples can help, but that recipe was unstable. One possible cause is that it took about half as many gradient steps. Learning the column remapping (r1c3, 0.02) failed: PPO did not find the mirror in time. This round: (A) 3 epochs, a middle setting for more samples with the same number of gradient steps; (B) 2 epochs with many small minibatches, to restore gradient steps, and the default entropy; (C) A's recipe plus a wider head that also sees global context, so A and C isolate the head change.

### Round 3
Flipping the trunk features left-right before the footprint pool head solves the mirror rule: every mirror run learns, and the learned column-mixing head (r1c3) did not. The best result is r2c2 (0.946). It uses the same flip network with 2 PPO epochs, 64 minibatches and gamma 0.97, so it gets more fresh designs and enough gradient steps. Its two seeds agree closely (0.945, 0.947). Its training success was still rising at the end (0.825 to 0.918), so it is probably short of samples. At 3 epochs, adding global context to the head raised dev success from 0.738 to 0.857, a gap much larger than the seed spread. In r1c2, fewer gradient steps caused one seed to fail (0.078). This round tests three things: r2c2's recipe with the global-context head; 1 epoch with small minibatches, which gives about 1.85x more samples and similar gradient steps; and a higher learning rate for faster learning within the same budget.

### Round 4
The left-right flip of trunk features before the footprint pool head is what makes learning work: without it, scores stay at 0, and a learned column mixer (r1c3) failed. The recipe is the next biggest lever. Two PPO epochs with 64 minibatches and gamma 0.97 lifted the score from about 0.74 to about 0.95 (r2c2 0.946, r3c3 0.949; seeds within 0.03 of each other). Two runs that cut gradient steps had a seed collapse (r1c2 and r3c2, one epoch). Doubling lr to 0.002 sped up early learning: training success was 0.17 at 25% of training versus 0.006. Training success was still rising at the end, so learning speed still limits these runs. The global-context head was no better under the good recipe (0.928). The remaining dev failures are few, and the best runs place almost nothing outside the target (0.10 cells per episode), so the last errors are probably about build order or the final brick. With one round left, I'm making safe, single-change recipe refinements of r3c3.

## Trial it ended with
name: Mirror head, r2c2 recipe, lr 0.002
hypothesis: Same as r2c2, but with the learning rate doubled to 0.002. r2c2's training success first rose only between 25% and 50% of training and was still climbing at the end, so the run is limited by learning speed.
